evidence.excerpt: Boards intended for environments with frequent thermal excursions require design-for-testability decisions that balance initial test coverage with the need to maintain that coverage throughout the product lifetime as solder joints and contact pads degrade. This preprint consolidates data from five years of thermal cycling experiments and production test monitoring at two electronics manufacturing partners to derive a set of quantitative DFT guidelines. For each of twelve layout and routing decisions—including test pad size, via-in-pad avoidance, and scan chain segmentation—the study reports the effect on initial boundary-scan coverage, estimated coverage at 1,000 thermal cycles, and the probability of a probe contact failure per 100,000 test operations. The guidelines are expressed as scoring criteria compatible with standard DFT review checklists. Validation on three new board designs showed that following the guidelines improved predicted 1,000-cycle coverage by an average of 9.4 percentage points relative to designs reviewed without the guidelines.
